doc.title: Bill Mays interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 5, 2025

title: Unprepared in Australia with Rosemary Clooney
summary: Subbing for Clooney's pianist, he lacked the big band scores and was rescued by the house bandleader; the lesson is preparation against stage fright.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: I’ll tell you – it wasn’t a train wreck, this was a real learning experience about being prepared. I was very young, Rosemary Clooney’s pianist, Paul Moore, got sick and couldn’t make the gig in Australia. And I got the call, through her drummer. And I’d never worked with a big band. And I hadn’t worked with that many singers. And I didn’t think, I just didn’t know, and nobody told me, call their office and get the scores to the big band charts that you’re going to be playing and you’re going to be counting and conducting. I didn’t know to do that. And we got to Australia and we went to the first rehearsal and I had no idea what to do. And I was terribly embarrassed. And the house band leader came to my rescue and led the rehearsal and that was a real lesson to me, “Dummy, prepare properly in advance.” That was a train wreck in my mind. That was a very embarrassing situation and frightened me, and I had to deal with it in therapy for a while to move past that.
Yeah, I’ll bet it never happened to you again.

It didn’t. And you know I talk to young people in clinics informally about stage fright. And I talk about this aspect. I say, “You know often we feel nervous if we’re not prepared.” If we had the music in advance and we thought we had it covered and whoops here’s a difficult passage that we should have written the fingering down for and put a metronome on and played it at tempo and nailed it in advance so that you’re comfortable with it in performance.
